authority: CEO R325 §P7 — cemetery packages as part of the product

P-14.negative_knowledge: CSF flow variability (posture, activity, circadian) creates noise that fundamentally limits yield estimation. Signal-to-noise ceiling is ~18%, not the 30% target.
P-14.falsification_evidence: R308: 16.5% vs 30% target. R319 diagnosis: mechanism failure (CSF flow noise floor). No repair possible.
P-14.failure_mechanism: The yield signal is smaller than the CSF flow noise. No estimator design can overcome this SNR limitation.
P-14.applicability_boundary: Applies to ALL yield-matching or flow-estimation candidates in CSF. Does NOT apply to candidates that don't estimate yield (e.g., P-01 uses direct pressure, not yield estimation).
P-14.future_candidate_prohibition: Do not manufacture yield-matching candidates with SNR < 2. Calculate SNR = (expected signal range) / (CSF flow variability) before manufacturing.

P-17.negative_knowledge: Endothelial cells cannot survive long-term in CSF. CSF lacks blood perfusion (nutrient supply) and has insufficient growth factors.
P-17.falsification_evidence: R308: endothelial survival 0.215 vs 0.3 threshold. R319 diagnosis: mechanism failure (biological constraint, not engineering).
P-17.failure_mechanism: CSF is not a growth medium. Endothelial cells require blood perfusion for nutrients. Without vascularization (impossible in a shunt catheter), cells die.
P-17.applicability_boundary: Applies to ALL cellular surfaces in CSF. Does NOT apply to synthetic surfaces (P-20 glycan is synthetic, not cellular) or non-CSF environments.
P-17.future_candidate_prohibition: Do not manufacture cellular surfaces for CSF without verifying cell viability in CSF-like conditions for >30 days. Consider ependymal cells (native to CSF) or synthetic alternatives.

P-19.negative_knowledge: Distributed multi-channel drainage does NOT provide obstruction resilience beyond baseline conductance matching. Under 3D Navier-Stokes with matched baseline, single channel BEATS distributed (13.88 vs 19.75 mmHg at 50% obstruction).
P-19.falsification_evidence: R322: conductance-matched decisive test. Baseline matched (9.87 vs 9.83 mmHg, 0.4%). Under 50% obstruction: single 13.88, distributed 19.75. Single wins. 1D Poiseuille predicted equal; 3D shows single is better.
P-19.failure_mechanism: At matched baseline conductance, the single channel's very low resistance (R/30) gives it more headroom under obstruction. The distributed architecture's per-channel velocity increases more under obstruction (each remaining channel carries more flow), creating higher Poiseuille resistance. 1D model missed this because it doesn't capture velocity-dependent resistance.
P-19.applicability_boundary: Applies to ALL distributed-vs-single hydraulic comparisons. Does NOT apply to non-hydraulic distributed systems (e.g., distributed computing, distributed sensing).
P-19.future_candidate_prohibition: Do not manufacture distributed-channel candidates without conductance-matched 3D verification (KA-009). 1D Poiseuille is INSUFFICIENT for this comparison — 3D effects can reverse the conclusion.
P-19.falsification_chain: 11 rounds (R312-R322): manufacture → metric flaw → metric redesign → threshold sensitivity → parameter uncertainty → external solver → matched obstruction → conductance matching → FALSIFICATION
